title: iG-kway: Incremental k-way Graph Partitioning on GPU
problem: Graph partitioning is critical in CAD applications, where circuit graphs undergo iterative incremental modifications during optimization, but existing GPU-accelerated partitioners (like G-kway) only support full re-partitioning from scratch.
motivation: Incremental graph partitioning enables faster design optimization iterations by updating only affected vertices rather than re-partitioning entire graphs, critical for iterative CAD flows.
method: iG-kway is the first GPU-based incremental k-way graph partitioner. It features an incrementality-aware data structure that efficiently tracks and updates only affected vertices, combined with a specialized refinement kernel that processes changed regions with minimal quality loss. The design is compared against G-kway on CAD-relevant graph partitioning benchmarks.
key_novelty: GPU-accelerated incremental k-way graph partitioning with specialized data structures for efficient vertex-level updates during iterative optimization.
contributions: First GPU-based incremental k-way graph partitioner
Incrementality-aware data structure for efficient updates
Specialized refinement kernel minimizing quality loss
84x speedup over G-kway with comparable partitioning quality
primary_theme: Incremental GPU-accelerated graph partitioning for iterative CAD
